attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet point in his signed post.

semantics.note: Unhedged present-tense observation. Narrowing it to LLM expectations fits the surrounding bullet about putting LLMs into production.

contract.note: Choosing Oct–Dec 2023 as the period and requiring a before-and-after revision is a reasonable plain reading. The speaker named no period or measure, so the drafter's interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: Deloitte Q4 2023 survey of Gen AI broadly. It shows high expectations, but there is no earlier wave to compare against, so it cannot show whether expectations were revised.
BCG survey shows dissatisfaction alongside continued optimism. It has no matched comparison of expectations and covers AI broadly, not LLMs.

reviews.rationale: Neither survey compares the same companies' earlier and later expectations, and neither shows which initial expectations were unrealistic. Their mix of high expectations and dissatisfaction neither establishes nor rules out a pattern of downward revision.

semantics.note: 'Will be' is an unhedged forecast with no deadline. Tying it to training-data sources follows the clause about sources and their legality.

contract.note: Reading 'major issue' as consequential litigation, and resolving early on a landmark class settlement, is a fair, ordinary plain reading. Absence of such a case is not treated as failure.

evidence.note: Court memorandum filed 2025-10-17 records preliminary approval of the Bartz v. Anthropic settlement over pirated source books. The court calls it the largest copyright class settlement in history, and the filing predates the evaluation date.

reviews.rationale: The forecast had no deadline, but the contract's early-resolution rule is met. In September 2025 a court gave preliminary approval to a record class-wide settlement over a major AI developer's acquisition of source material, which shows litigation became a major issue.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to turn stated uncertainty into a specific financial claim. There is no company, profit measure or period to test against.

reviews.rationale: 'In question' expresses uncertainty about the industry's economics. It names no company, measure or period, so no observed outcome could confirm or refute it without adding commitments the speaker did not make. The packet also has no evidence items.

semantics.note: An observation about GPT-4's first year. 'Substantial progress' is a fair rendering of 'lots of progress'.

contract.note: Plain reading: multiple real deployments to users during the year after GPT-4's launch. This is an ordinary reading, neither stretched for nor against the speaker.

evidence.note: Company disclosure dated 2023-03-14. Two GPT-4 features were available immediately in a paid tier, so this is an actual deployment, not just an announcement.
Company disclosure dated 2023-09-25. A GPT-4 assistant was tested by more than 19,000 beta users and then rolled out as an open beta, inside the target period.

reviews.rationale: Two separate GPT-4 applications, language tutoring and visual assistance for blind users, reached real users within the year. That meets the support condition. Both sources are the companies' own disclosures, but they document product availability, as the contract's source requirements prefer.
